messages:
Maya: Pushed a new spin on the private setup preflight UI in Figma. Focused on making failures actionable without overwhelming the user. Link: https://fig.ma/redwood/preflight-v2 :frame_with_picture:
Samir: skimmed it. big +1 for fewer modals. One thought: the inline pills that show failures are a bit wordy. Can we have a one-line summary + a chevron to expand details?
Eli: yes — summary headline in plain language, then a collapsed panel with technical detail (command + machine code). e.g. 'S3 access blocked — (network.S3_TCP_REFUSED)'. Keep the machine code hidden by default.
Maya: mock shows that — headline first, small muted code beneath in expanded view. Also added a tiny copy icon next to shells so support can paste commands into terminal.
Frank: color/accessibility check: failed pill background contrast is 3.2:1 against white. We need to hit 4.5:1. Suggest using token red-600 on surface or add a subtle left border + icon so color isn't the only signal.
A11yBot: Accessibility note: use icon + text label. Ensure the failure pill is keyboard-focusable (tab index) and has aria-expanded when it can open details. Announce state changes via an aria-live region.
Samir: Regarding state updates: should checks auto-poll or be manual? Auto is friendlier but noisy for screenreader users. Maybe manual by default and an opt-in 'auto watch' toggle.
Eli: Agreed. If auto is enabled, throttle updates and group messages into a single announcement: 'Network checks updated: 2 passed, 1 failed' instead of announcing each check.
Maya: I also experimented with a 'what this means' micro-link on each failure pill that opens the KB anchored to that error. That KB should show exact hostnames/ports we tested so customers can copy the lines into firewall rules.
Frank: Good. For copyable CLI, include an accessible label: aria-label="Copy network diagnostic command" and role="button". Also make the copied string include a comment with the failing hostname so support has context.
Maya: example snippet in the mock:

```bash
# run on customer host to test outbound
curl -sS https://s3.redwood.ai/health || echo "connect failed to s3.redwood.ai"
```

Maya: copy button text should be 'Copy command' not just an icon tooltip.
Samir: Microcopy change: 'Retry preflight' feels scary. Use 'Re-run checks' or 'Check again'. 'Re-run' mirrors developer language.
Eli: Also recommend showing an at-a-glance summary line at top of the step: 'Network checks: 4 passed, 1 failed' that links to the failed item. This helps keyboard and screenreader users jump to the issue.
A11yBot: For the summary, include aria-live="polite" and update the text after the whole batch finishes. Provide skip links for keyboard users: 'Skip to failed check'.
Maya: UX question: when a check fails, should we auto-expand the troubleshooting panel or leave it collapsed? Thoughts?
Frank: Auto-expanding can be helpful but might be disruptive if multiple checks fail. Maybe expand the first failing check only and show a 'show all' control.
Samir: Fine by me. Also include a short one-line remediation suggestion inline e.g., 'Allow outbound TCP 443 to s3.redwood.ai' then 'More troubleshooting' to expand deeper steps.
Eli: For telemetry, emit both a human-readable status and a machine code (e.g., network.DNS_TIMEOUT) so support flows can map quickly. Show only the human text and hide the code in details.
Maya: I'll add that to the design doc. Also planning a small toast after re-run completes: 'Checks complete — 5 passed, 1 failed'. A11yBot, ok to show toast?
A11yBot: Toast ok if it updates the aria-live summary and is dismissible via keyboard. Keep a longer timeout (5s+) and don't rely on it for critical messaging.
OpsBot: deploy-bot:preflight-check kicked off for maya/preflight-v2 at 1781234000
Maya: Next actions: Frank to propose accessible color tokens and icon set, Eli to draft the concise summary + machine code pattern, Samir to change CTA labels, I'll update Figma and the KB anchors.
Frank: will drop tokens and icon recommendations by EOD. :white_check_mark:
Eli: drafting summary copy now, will link here when done.
Maya: thanks team — will post updated screenshot when merged.
